topic.title: LEGO Lost DKK 1.4 Billion in 2003. Then It Went Back to the Brick

title: LEGO Almost Went Broke, and Kids Still Loved the Brick
description:
Why did LEGO almost go broke while kids still loved the brick?
The toy maker had drifted far from the brick; going back to it turned the company around.
Sources: The Motley Fool, The LEGO Group (Dec 2025).
Based on public records and reporting. Not financial or legal advice.

lines.text: LEGO almost went broke, while kids never stopped loving the brick.
In one year, the company behind it lost about DKK 1.4B. So where did the money go?
Not into the brick. LEGO had poured itself into theme parks, like this one in its home town, Billund.
And its boxes had filled up with new, one-off pieces, far too many to make cheaply. So what could save it?
Then a young new boss, Jørgen Vig Knudstorp, took LEGO back to the brick, and sold control of the parks.
Today LEGO shops run from Billund to London to Singapore.
Last year, it sold DKK 83.5B worth of toys, 12% more than the year before.
And it kept DKK 16.7B of that for itself, from the same plastic brick it nearly gave up on.
Brick or theme park: which would you have kept? Because not long ago,
